faq.q: What is the origin of Shakila?
faq.a: Shakila is associated with Arabic. Shakila is Arabic شَكِيلَة (Shakīla), the feminine of شَكِيل, meaning 'handsome, well-formed'.
Yes — the underlying form شَكِيلَة is Arabic.
Shakila can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Shakila should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Shakīla is not a Quranic personal name.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Shakila, shakila. Script forms are شَكِيلَة, شکیله, شکیلہ, शकीला.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
